searchText: <@!363800010518822915> <@!203220829473996800>, here's the fork choice tests as YAML, as I mentioned this morning: https://gist.github.com/paulhauner/c7b71e50d25e679d36726167d11bebcb they're not polished, but i've found them very useful in testng they're generated here. little ascii tree diagrams included :) https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/blob/proto-array/eth2/proto_array_fork_choice/src/fork_choice_test_definition.rs <@!361447803194441738> nice work 👏 What is the rationale for using the Validator Key to issue the Voluntary Exit? As opposed to the withdrawal key. In the case of the latter, a staking service could generate, keep safe and propose/attestate blocks with its VK on behalf of a customer, while the customer generates and keeps the WK in a very safe place, until they decide to perform such voluntary exit. is anyone working on the validator APIs? in particular it looks like we will want to extend the validator APIs to also pass in the domain for a given operation actually it looks like the minimal data the beacon node should provide is the current data under `state.fork` for the current beacon state the validator client can then recompute the rest of it wondering if anyone else has run into this yet PR being discussed here ! https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/pull/15 haven;t discussed fork stuff though yeah it seems like we will want to get the fork bytes from the beacon node thats the "trust minimized" approach Yeah our validator polls for the for each epoch otherwise we can just take the domain from the beacon node *for the Fork gotcha thanks!
